pool.q: What do all-electric vehicles (battery electric vehicles, BEVs) have instead of an internal combustion engine?
pool.explain: The motor is powered by a large traction battery that is charged from the grid.
pool.evidence: All-electric vehicles, also referred to as battery electric vehicles (BEVs), have an electric motor instead of an internal combustion engine.

pool.q: What does EVSE stand for?
options: Electric vehicle supply equipment — the charging equipment
pool.explain: BEVs must be plugged into a wall outlet or EVSE to charge.
pool.evidence: charging equipment , also called electric vehicle supply equipment (EVSE)

pool.q: Why are all-electric vehicles classed as zero-emission vehicles?
options: They produce no direct exhaust or tailpipe emissions locally
They are built from recycled parts
pool.explain: Emissions from generating the electricity happen elsewhere.
pool.evidence: categorizes all-electric vehicles as zero-emission vehicles because they produce no direct exhaust or tailpipe emissions locally

pool.q: In an electric drive vehicle, what does the auxiliary battery power?
pool.explain: The large traction battery pack powers the motor.
pool.evidence: the auxiliary battery provides electricity to power vehicle accessories

pool.q: Which components does an all-electric vehicle not have?
options: Liquid fuel parts such as a fuel pump, fuel line or fuel tank
pool.explain: It runs entirely on electricity.
pool.evidence: does not contain the typical liquid fuel components, such as a fuel pump, fuel line, or fuel tank

pool.q: What battery warranties are several EV manufacturers offering?
pool.explain: Batteries are designed for extended life but eventually wear out.
pool.evidence: Several manufacturers of electric vehicles are offering 8-year/100,000-mile battery warranties.

pool.q: How do EV energy and purchase costs compare with similar conventional vehicles?
options: Energy costs are usually lower, but purchase prices can be much higher
pool.explain: Incentives and lower running costs can offset the higher price.
pool.evidence: Although energy costs for EVs are generally lower than for similar conventional vehicles, purchase prices can be significantly higher.

pool.q: Why are battery prices expected to keep falling?
options: Battery technology is improving and production volumes are rising
pool.explain: Cheaper batteries narrow the price gap with conventional cars.
pool.evidence: Battery prices are expected to continue declining as battery technologies improve and production volumes increase.

pool.q: Do EV batteries last forever?
options: They must be replaced every year
No — they're built for a long life but will wear out eventually
pool.explain: Many makers offer 8-year/100,000-mile battery warranties.
pool.evidence: The advanced batteries in electric vehicles are designed for extended life but will wear out eventually.

pool.q: Which are the main challenges with nickel-metal hydride batteries?
options: High cost, high self-discharge, heat generation at high temperatures and controlling hydrogen loss
They are too light to use in cars
pool.explain: Lithium-ion batteries dominate EVs today for their energy density and life.
pool.evidence: The main challenges with nickel-metal hydride batteries are their high cost, high self-discharge rate, heat generation at high temperatures, and the need to control hydrogen loss.

pool.q: Why are lithium-ion batteries used in most portable electronics?
options: They store a lot of energy per unit of mass and volume
pool.explain: The same property makes them the leading choice for EVs.
pool.evidence: because of their high energy per unit mass and volume relative to other electrical energy storage systems

pool.q: What are advanced high-power lead-acid batteries used for in commercial EVs?
pool.explain: Lead-acid batteries are heavy for the energy they store.
pool.evidence: these batteries are only used in commercially available electric vehicles for ancillary loads

pool.q: Why is the chemical identity of an atom so stable?
options: The protons in its nucleus are extremely hard to dislodge
Neutrons hold the electrons in place
pool.explain: Chemistry happens through electrons, not protons.
pool.evidence: The protons in an atom's nucleus are extremely difficult to dislodge, and so the chemical identity of any atom is very stable.

pool.q: What do atoms form when they are joined by chemical bonds?
options: Molecules with their own unique properties
pool.explain: Bonds are links formed by electrons.
pool.evidence: When atoms are joined by chemical bonds, they form materials with unique properties known as molecules

pool.q: What happens when ionic bonds form from neutral atoms?
pool.explain: The atoms end up positively and negatively charged.
pool.evidence: When ionic bonds are formed from neutral atoms, there is a transfer of electrons between the positively and negatively charged atoms.

pool.q: What is unusual about lead dioxide?
options: It is a gas at room temperature
It is metallic and conducts electricity, unlike most metal oxides
pool.explain: This matters for how lead-acid cells work.
pool.evidence: lead dioxide is metallic and is an electrical conductor, unlike other metal oxides that are usually insulators

pool.q: In electricity, what is a 'battery'?
options: A set of voltaic cells designed to give more voltage and/or current than one cell alone
A capacitor in a power supply
pool.explain: Cells in series raise voltage; cells in parallel raise current capacity.
pool.evidence: In electricity, a "battery" is a set of voltaic cells designed to provide greater voltage and/or current than is possible with one cell alone.

pool.q: How do you get more voltage than a single cell can provide?
pool.explain: Cell size affects capacity, not voltage.
pool.evidence: To obtain greater voltage than the output of a single cell, multiple cells must be connected in series.

pool.q: What are the electrodes in large batteries often called?
pool.explain: They are commonly thin metal grids or plates.
pool.evidence: are often referred to as plates instead of electrodes

pool.q: Why is a fuel cell far less polluting than normal combustion?
options: It operates far below combustion temperature, so no nitrogen oxides form
It uses no fuel at all
pool.explain: A fuel cell harnesses the chemical reaction of combustion at a low temperature.
pool.evidence: Because the operating temperature of modern fuel cells is far below that of normal combustion, no oxides of nitrogen (NO x ) are formed

pool.q: What was the mercury standard cell used for?
pool.explain: It gave a very stable reference voltage.
pool.evidence: a special type of battery known as a mercury standard cell was popularly used as a voltage calibration standard

pool.q: Why could standard cells only be measured with a null-balance (potentiometric) device?
options: Almost no current could be drawn from them
pool.explain: Even small currents disturbed their accuracy.
pool.evidence: standard cells could only be measured with a potentiometric (null-balance) device where current drain is almost zero

pool.q: Is it safe to install and use home charging equipment outdoors, even when it rains?
options: No, charging must always be indoors
Only with a waterproof cover over the car
Yes — outdoor installation and use are safe, even when charging in the rain
pool.explain: Choose safety-certified equipment and a certified electrical contractor.
pool.evidence: outdoor installation and use are also safe, even if the vehicle is being charged in the rain.

pool.q: How does the US National Electrical Code treat EV charging?
pool.explain: Contractors must size circuits accordingly.
pool.evidence: EV charging infrastructure is considered a continuous load by the National Electrical Code (NEC).

pool.q: What is recommended when buying home charging equipment?
options: Safety-certified equipment and a certified electrical contractor
pool.explain: ENERGY STAR chargers are tested by a recognised laboratory.
pool.evidence: Purchasing safety-certified equipment is recommended

pool.q: What is the first step when planning to procure and install charging infrastructure?
options: Considering your community members and their expected charging needs
Installing as many chargers as possible
pool.explain: Travel patterns, EV ownership and charging times determine what to build where.
pool.evidence: The first step when planning to procure and install charging infrastructure is to consider your community members.

pool.q: Which information helps decide how many and what type of chargers a project needs?
options: Only the number of parking spaces
Expected charging needs: travel patterns, EV ownership, charging times and vehicle types
pool.explain: Planning starts with the community's needs.
pool.evidence: It is important to understand their expected charging needs based on travel patterns, EV ownership

pool.q: With whom should charging infrastructure projects be designed?
options: A diverse set of community members
pool.explain: Access for all types of communities matters.
pool.evidence: It is important to design charging infrastructure projects alongside a diverse set of community members.

pool.q: Who must complete charging station installations?
options: A licensed electrical contractor, in line with local and state codes
pool.explain: Chargers should also meet standards such as SAE J1772.
pool.evidence: Charging station installations must comply with local and state codes and regulations and be completed by a licensed electrical contractor.

pool.q: Which SAE standard should charging infrastructure comply with?
pool.explain: Standards make chargers and vehicles compatible.
pool.evidence: Charging infrastructure should also be compliant with SAE International standards, such as SAE J1772.

pool.q: What is an advantage of a site host owning its charging stations?
options: Full control over the station and all its revenue
pool.explain: The host also pays to buy, install and maintain them.
pool.evidence: which allows for full control over the station and the ability to keep all revenue from the station

pool.q: What must an electrical contractor get before installing charging infrastructure?
options: A letter from the car maker
A permit from the local building authorities
pool.explain: Installations must follow local and state codes.
pool.evidence: obtain a permit from the local building authorities before installing charging infrastructure

pool.q: How do maintenance needs of plug-in hybrids (PHEVs) and hybrids (HEVs) compare with conventional vehicles?
options: They are similar, because these vehicles also have internal combustion engines
They need no maintenance at all
pool.explain: All-electric vehicles have fewer fluids and moving parts, so they need less maintenance.
pool.evidence: Because PHEVs and HEVs have internal combustion engines, maintenance requirements are similar to those of conventional vehicles.

pool.q: Why do brakes on electric vehicles generally last longer?
pool.explain: The motor slows the car and recovers energy, so the brakes do less work.
pool.evidence: brake systems generally last longer than those on conventional vehicles because of regenerative braking

pool.q: What is a battery's 'cycle life'?
options: The number of times it can be charged and discharged
pool.explain: Advanced batteries have a limited number of cycles.
pool.evidence: the number of times the battery can be charged and discharged

pool.q: Why do all-electric vehicles need less maintenance?
options: They are serviced by the grid
They have fewer moving parts and fluids to change
pool.explain: Plug-in hybrids still need engine maintenance.
pool.evidence: all-electric vehicles require less maintenance because they have fewer moving parts and fluids to change

pool.q: Why must hazardous energy be controlled (lockout/tagout) during servicing?
options: Workers servicing machines may be seriously injured or killed if it is not properly controlled
pool.explain: Energy sources must be isolated and locked out before maintenance — including high-voltage EV systems.
pool.evidence: Workers servicing or maintaining machines or equipment may be seriously injured or killed if hazardous energy is not properly controlled.

pool.q: Which accident shows the danger of uncontrolled hazardous energy?
options: A worker tripping over a cable
A jammed conveyor suddenly releasing and crushing a worker clearing it
pool.explain: Lockout/tagout prevents stored energy being released during work.
pool.evidence: A jammed conveyor system suddenly releases, crushing a worker who is trying to clear the jam.

pool.q: What happened in the steam valve example?
options: The valve turned on automatically and burned workers repairing a pipe
Nothing — the valve was locked out
pool.explain: Equipment must be isolated and locked before servicing.
pool.evidence: A steam valve is automatically turned on burning workers who are repairing a downstream connection in the piping.
